summary_paragraph: The patient with complex post–Roux-en-Y gastric bypass history (including bypass reversal) and gastrostomy tube dependence presented with 3 days of epigastric burning pain radiating to the esophagus consistent with severe reflux symptoms. Initial evaluation included abdominal radiographs showing a non-obstructive bowel gas pattern without free air. She was treated with IV proton pump inhibitor therapy, cholestyramine, antiemetics, and continuation of erythromycin for gastric dysmotility while tube feeds and a stage 3 diet were maintained and adjusted for nutritional needs. Gastroenterology recommended adding ranitidine and performing EGD, which demonstrated post-surgical anatomy with traversable angulation (no obstruction), small clean-based ulcerations with friability at the gastro-gastric anastomosis, and antral erythema consistent with gastritis. With improvement in symptoms and oral intake, tube feeds were decreased back to outpatient rate, home medications were resumed, and she was discharged home with services on pantoprazole increased to twice daily plus cholestyramine and ranitidine, with follow-up already scheduled.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation
